title: Background chip, round 2 — the Subagents chip's look, and a Stop button to pick

steps.path: A Claude Code conversation with commands left running → the bottom bar
steps.headline: The Background chip now looks like the Subagents chip: an icon first, then one count in words.
steps.changed: "Background ● 2 ● 1 ✓ 1" is now "⠋ 2 commands" — the same moving icon and wording the Subagents chip uses. While anything is running, that is the only number. Once everything has ended it reads "1 failed · 3 finished" with a red or check icon first, the way the Subagents chip does.
steps.notice: Every number has its word beside it, so there is nothing to decode. The full breakdown is in the popup's title line and the chip's hover text.
steps.risk: While commands are running, a failed one is not counted on the chip until everything has ended; you see it in the popup. When nothing is running, "3 finished" doesn't say "commands", same as the Subagents chip — side by side, they are told apart by position and hover text.

steps.headline: At phone width the chip keeps its words, exactly like the Subagents chip beside it.
steps.changed: The first version dropped the word and showed just dots and numbers. Now it says "⠋ 1 command" at every width.
steps.notice: The two chips read the same way on a phone.
steps.risk: Slightly wider than the dot-only version, so on a very crowded bar it may move to the second line sooner.

steps.path: Claude Code conversation → click the Background chip
steps.headline: Each row's status label now sits at the top right, level with the command's name.
steps.changed: The Running / Watching / Failed / Finished label was centred on the row's height; it now lines up with the first line, as on the Subagents popup's cards.
steps.notice: The name and its state read as one line, top to bottom.
steps.risk: None expected — only the label's height in the row moved.

steps.path: Native conversation → click the Background chip → a running command
steps.headline: Which Stop button should a running command's row have?
steps.notice: Whichever you pick, it does the same thing: ends the command and everything it started, without asking first, exactly like the Stop on its card. Only native conversations get it.

variants.label: Filled, in the label's place
variants.summary: The first version: a solid accent-coloured Stop where the Running label would be.
variants.risk: The loudest thing in the popup, and there is no Running label beside it.

variants.label: Outlined, in the label's place
variants.summary: The same spot, drawn as an outlined button — the look of the Stop on the Subagents popup's cards.
variants.risk: No Running label; the row's section heading is what says it is running.

variants.label: Running label + outlined Stop
variants.summary: Keeps the green Running label every other row has, with an outlined Stop to its right.
variants.risk: Takes the most room; a long command name wraps a little sooner.

variants.label: Running label + stop icon
variants.summary: The Running label, then a small round stop symbol. Hovering shows "Stop this command".
variants.risk: The smallest target, and on a phone there is no hover text, so the symbol has to speak for itself. It is the same symbol the Stopped label uses.
